instructions: Beat the eggs with the milk and a good grind of black pepper.
Toast the sourdough and keep warm.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over a low heat, add the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula until softly set.
Remove from the heat and fold through the torn smoked salmon and most of the snipped chives.
Pile onto the toast and scatter with the remaining chives.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and soften the sliced onion and pepper for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin and chipotle paste, cook for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and drained beans and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Make four hollows in the sauce, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until the whites are set.
Meanwhile, warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan.
Serve the eggs and sauce over the tortillas, topped with crumbled feta and coriander.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, oil, vanilla and lemon zest together, then pour into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Fold in the blueberries and divide the batter between the cases.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until risen, golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Mix the oats with the apple juice and yoghurt in a bowl.
Grate in the apple, including the skin, and stir well.
Cover and chill overnight.
In the morning, loosen with a splash more juice if needed, then serve topped with the raspberries, almonds and a drizzle of honey.
Melt half the butter in a small frying pan and fry the sliced mushrooms for 4 minutes until golden.
Add the spinach and stir until just wilted, then tip onto a plate.
Beat the eggs with a little seasoning.
Melt the remaining butter in the pan, pour in the eggs and cook, drawing the edges in towards the centre, until almost set.
Scatter the mushrooms, spinach and grated cheese over one half, fold over and slide onto a plate.
Blend the banana, eggs, oats, baking powder and cinnamon in a blender until smooth.
Leave the batter to stand for 5 minutes to thicken.
Heat a little of the coconut oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat.
Cook spoonfuls of the batter for 2 minutes on each side until golden, adding more oil as needed.
Serve topped with the yoghurt and blueberries.
Heat the grill to high, put the kippers flesh-side up on a foil-lined tray and dot with the butter.
Grill for 4 to 5 minutes until hot through.
Meanwhile, bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer, add the vinegar and poach the eggs for 3 minutes.
Toast the bread.
Serve the kippers with the eggs and toast, with a squeeze of lemon and a scattering of chopped parsley.
Boil the sliced potatoes for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Heat the oil in a 24 cm ovenproof frying pan and fry the sliced onion and pepper for 8 minutes, then add the potatoes.
Heat the grill to high.
Beat the eggs with the grated parmesan, chopped parsley and seasoning, pour into the pan and cook over a low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until mostly set.
Grill for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and set on top, then cut into wedges.
Whisk the chia seeds, almond milk, maple syrup and vanilla together in a bowl.
Leave for 10 minutes, then whisk again to break up any clumps.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight until thick.
Spoon into glasses and top with the diced mango and passion fruit pulp.
Mix the flours, yeast and sugar in a bowl, then beat in the milk and water to make a smooth batter.
Cover and leave in a warm place for 1 hour until bubbly.
Dissolve the bicarbonate of soda and salt in 2 tbsp warm water and beat into the batter, then leave for 10 minutes.
Heat a heavy frying pan over a medium-low heat, lightly oil the pan and a few crumpet rings, and add enough batter to fill each ring halfway.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the tops are set and full of holes, then remove the rings, flip and cook for 1 minute more.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the chopped onion, carrots, celery and apple for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the rinsed lentils, stock and diced chicken, bring to the boil and simmer for 25 minutes.
Lift out the chicken, blend the soup until smooth, then return the chicken with the coconut milk.
Heat through, squeeze in the lemon juice and season to taste.
Heat the oil in a large pan and soften the chopped onion for 5 minutes.
Add the ground coriander and cook for 1 minute.
Add the sliced carrots, diced potato and stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the carrots are very tender.
Add most of the fresh coriander and blend until smooth.
Season and serve scattered with the remaining coriander.
Melt the butter in a large pan and gently cook the chopped onion, celery and leek for 10 minutes.
Add the diced potato and stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the broccoli florets and chopped stalk and simmer for 5 minutes until just tender.
Blend until smooth, then crumble in most of the stilton and stir until melted.
Season with black pepper and serve topped with the remaining stilton.
Bring the stock to a simmer and add the bruised lemongrass, sliced galangal, torn lime leaves and bruised chillies.
Simmer for 10 minutes to infuse.
Add the sliced mushrooms and halved tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until pink.
Remove from the heat, stir in the fish sauce and lime juice to taste and serve scattered with coriander.
Roughly chop the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, onion and garlic.
Soak the bread in a little cold water for 5 minutes, then squeeze dry.
Blend the vegetables and bread with 3 tbsp of the oil, the vinegar and salt until very smooth.
Pass through a sieve for an extra-silky soup if you like, then chill for at least 2 hours.
Serve very cold, drizzled with the remaining oil.
Melt the butter in a large pan and gently cook the chopped onion for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the diced potatoes, milk and bay leaf and simmer for 10 minutes until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Lay the haddock in the pan and poach for 5 minutes, then lift out, remove the skin and flake into large pieces.
Lightly crush some of the potatoes to thicken the soup, then return the fish with the cream and warm through.
Season with black pepper and serve scattered with snipped chives.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Roughly chop the peppers and onion, toss with the unpeeled garlic and oil in a roasting tin and roast for 30 minutes until soft and charred.
Squeeze the garlic from its skins and tip everything into a pan with the paprika, tomatoes and stock.
Simmer for 10 minutes, then blend until smooth and season.
Serve with a swirl of crème fraîche and torn basil.
Melt the butter in a large pan and gently cook the chopped onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic.
Add the sliced mushrooms and thyme leaves and cook for 10 minutes until the mushrooms are soft and their liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually add the stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and season to taste.
Rub the chicken with 1 tbsp of the oil and the paprika and season.
Cook on a hot griddle or frying pan for 6 to 7 minutes on each side until cooked through, then rest and slice.
Whisk the remaining oil with the lime juice and honey.
Arrange the leaves, sliced avocado, halved tomatoes and thinly sliced onion on plates.
Top with the chicken and drizzle over the dressing.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Toss the cubed squash, chunked pepper and onion wedges with 2 tbsp of the oil and the cumin, then roast for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the quinoa and simmer in plenty of water for 12 to 15 minutes until tender, then drain well.
Whisk the remaining oil with the lemon juice and season.
Toss the quinoa with the roasted vegetables, spinach and dressing, then top with crumbled feta and the pumpkin seeds.
Cut the beetroot into wedges.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, then roughly chop.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and honey together and season.
Arrange the rocket and beetroot on plates and crumble over the goat's cheese.
Scatter with the walnuts and drizzle with the dressing.
Rub the steak with the oil and season, then cook in a very hot pan for 2 to 3 minutes on each side for medium-rare and rest for 5 minutes.
Mix the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and finely chopped chilli to make the dressing.
Combine the sliced cucumber, halved tomatoes, thinly sliced onion and the herbs in a bowl.
Thinly slice the steak and add to the salad with the dressing, tossing gently.
Serve scattered with the chopped peanuts.
Boil the halved potatoes for 12 to 15 minutes until tender, then drain and cool slightly.
Mix the crème fraîche, horseradish and lemon juice and season with black pepper.
Toss the warm potatoes with the dressing, sliced spring onions and chopped dill.
Flake the mackerel into large pieces, discarding the skin.
Serve the potatoes on the watercress, topped with the mackerel.
Put the couscous in a bowl, pour over the hot stock, cover and leave for 5 minutes, then fluff up with a fork.
Dice the cucumber and pepper, halve the tomatoes and slice the spring onions.
Whisk the oil with the lemon zest and juice and season.
Stir the vegetables, chopped mint and dressing through the couscous.
Crumble over the feta and serve.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), tear the pitta into pieces, toss with 1 tbsp of the oil and bake for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp.
Chop the lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, radishes and spring onions into bite-size pieces.
Roughly chop the parsley and mint leaves.
Whisk the remaining oil with the lemon juice, sumac and pomegranate molasses and season.
Toss everything together with the dressing and pitta crisps just before serving.
Boil the trimmed green beans for 4 minutes, then drain and cool under cold water.
Drain and rinse the kidney beans and chickpeas.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard and sugar together and season.
Toss the beans and chickpeas with the finely sliced onion, chopped parsley and dressing.
Leave for 10 minutes for the flavours to mingle before serving.
Toss the cubed beef in the seasoned flour and brown in batches in the oil in a large casserole, then set aside.
Fry the chopped onions, carrots and sliced mushrooms for 8 minutes, then return the beef.
Pour in the ale and stock, add the Worcestershire sauce and thyme, cover and simmer gently for 2 hours until tender, then leave to cool slightly.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), spoon the filling into a pie dish and cover with the pastry, pressing the edges to seal.
Brush with beaten egg, cut a steam hole and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until puffed and golden.
Heat the oil in a large pan and gently fry the finely chopped onions for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and korma paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the diced chicken and cook for 5 minutes, turning to coat.
Pour in the stock, stir in the ground almonds and coconut cream and simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove from the heat, stir in the yoghurt and scatter with coriander.
Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan).
Fry the lardons in 1 tbsp of the oil in a large casserole until crisp, then remove, and brown the floured, cubed beef in batches in the remaining oil.
Fry the chopped onion and carrots for 5 minutes, add the garlic and tomato purée, then return the beef and bacon with the wine, stock, bay and thyme.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook in the oven for 2 hours 30 minutes until the beef is very tender.
Brown the peeled shallots and mushrooms in the butter, stir them into the stew for the final 30 minutes and season before serving.
Pat the pork skin completely dry, score it in thin lines and rub the salt and crushed fennel seeds into the cuts.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan), sit the pork on the sliced onions and apples in a roasting tin and roast for 30 minutes.
Reduce the oven to 160°C (140°C fan), pour the cider and stock around the meat and roast for 2 hours more.
If the crackling needs crisping, turn the oven up to 230°C (210°C fan) for the final 15 minutes.
Rest the pork for 15 minutes, then mash the apples and onions into the pan juices to make a sauce.
Season the chicken and brown in the oil in a large casserole, then set aside.
Fry the sliced onion, pepper and mushrooms for 8 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and bubble for 2 minutes, then add the tomatoes and rosemary.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer gently for 40 minutes until tender.
Stir in the olives for the final 5 minutes and scatter with parsley before serving.
Mix the lamb with the grated onion, crushed garlic, spices, half the chopped mint and plenty of seasoning.
Shape into 12 sausage shapes, either around skewers or by hand, and chill for 15 minutes.
For the tzatziki, grate the cucumber, squeeze out the excess water and mix with the yoghurt, lemon juice and remaining mint.
Grill or griddle the koftas for 8 to 10 minutes, turning often, until browned and cooked through.
Serve in the warmed pittas with the tzatziki.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the cumin seeds until they sizzle.
Add the sliced onions, chunked peppers and slit chillies and stir-fry over a high heat for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, ground spices and salt and cook for 1 minute, then add the diced chicken and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce is thick.
Scatter with coriander and serve.
Mix the mince with the finely grated onion, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, egg yolk and plenty of seasoning.
Shape into four patties slightly wider than the buns and chill for 15 minutes.
Brush with the oil and cook in a hot griddle pan or on a barbecue for 4 to 5 minutes on each side.
Top each burger with a slice of cheese for the final minute to melt.
Serve in the toasted buns with lettuce, sliced tomato and red onion.
Melt the butter in a large pan and gently cook the sliced leeks for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the diced chicken and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the flour.
Gradually stir in the stock and milk and simmer for 15 minutes until thick and the chicken is cooked, then add the mustard and chopped tarragon and season.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), spoon the filling into a pie dish and cover with the pastry, crimping the edges.
Brush with beaten egg, cut a steam hole and bake for 30 minutes until golden.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), slice the aubergines, brush with 4 tbsp of the oil and roast for 25 minutes until soft and golden.
Fry the chopped onion and garlic in the remaining oil, add the mince and brown, then stir in the cinnamon, oregano, wine, tomatoes and purée and simmer for 30 minutes.
For the topping, melt the butter, stir in the flour, gradually whisk in the milk and simmer until thick, then cool slightly and beat in the eggs and half the grated parmesan.
Layer the aubergine and lamb sauce in a baking dish, pour over the topping and scatter with the remaining parmesan.
Reduce the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and bake for 45 minutes until golden, then rest for 15 minutes before serving.
Mix both minces with the finely grated onion, the breadcrumbs soaked in the milk, the egg, allspice and seasoning.
Roll into about 24 small balls.
Fry in the butter in batches for 8 to 10 minutes until browned all over and cooked through, then set aside.
Stir the flour into the pan juices, gradually add the stock and simmer for 3 minutes, then stir in the cream and soy sauce.
Return the meatballs to the sauce to warm through and serve with the lingonberry jam and mashed potatoes.

recipe-name: Jerk Chicken with Rice and Peas
instructions: Slash the chicken legs, rub all over with the jerk paste and lime juice and marinate for at least 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), drizzle the chicken with the oil and roast for 45 to 50 minutes until charred and cooked through.
Meanwhile, put the rinsed rice, coconut milk, water, drained beans, sliced spring onions, thyme, crushed garlic, whole scotch bonnet and salt in a pan.
Bring to the boil, cover tightly and cook over a low heat for 20 minutes until the rice is tender, then remove the chilli and thyme stalks.
Fluff up the rice and serve with the chicken.
Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan).
Mix the paprika, sugar, garlic granules, cumin and salt and rub all over the pork.
Put the pork in a deep roasting tin, pour the vinegar and water around it, cover tightly with foil and roast for 4 hours 30 minutes until falling apart.
Shred the meat with two forks, discarding the excess fat, and stir through the barbecue sauce and some of the pan juices.
Serve piled into the toasted buns.
Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, the tender part of the lemongrass and the soaked dried chillies to a paste.
Fry the paste in the oil in a heavy casserole for 8 minutes until fragrant and darkened.
Add the cubed beef, coconut milk, water, turmeric, tamarind, torn lime leaves, sugar and salt, then simmer uncovered over a low heat for 2 hours 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Toast the desiccated coconut in a dry pan until golden, then stir it into the curry.
Keep cooking for 30 minutes more, stirring often, until the sauce has almost completely evaporated and coats the beef.
Mix 2 tbsp of the soy sauce with the turmeric, ground coriander, 1 tbsp of the sugar and the oil, add the chicken strips and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Soak the skewers in water for 20 minutes, then thread on the chicken.
For the sauce, gently heat the peanut butter, coconut milk, curry paste and the remaining soy sauce and sugar, stirring until smooth, then add lime juice to taste.
Grill or griddle the skewers for 8 to 10 minutes, turning often, until charred and cooked through.
Serve with the satay sauce and sliced cucumber.
Slice the onions thinly and cook gently in the butter and half the oil for 15 minutes until soft and golden, then remove.
Cut the liver into strips and toss in the seasoned flour.
Fry the liver in the remaining oil over a high heat for 1 to 2 minutes on each side until browned but still slightly pink in the middle.
Return the onions with the stock, Worcestershire sauce and torn sage and bubble for 2 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Serve straight away with mashed potatoes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Fry the chopped onion and pepper in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Stir in the shredded chicken, drained beans and half the passata and season.
Mix the remaining passata with the chipotle paste and spread a little over the base of a baking dish.
Fill and roll the tortillas, lay them seam-side down in the dish, pour over the remaining sauce, top with the grated cheese and bake for 20 minutes, then serve with the soured cream.
Put the gammon in a large pan with the onion, carrot, bay and peppercorns, cover with cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 1 hour 40 minutes, skimming occasionally.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and lift the gammon into a roasting tin.
Cut away the skin, leaving a thin layer of fat, and score the fat in a diamond pattern, studding each diamond with a clove.
Mix the honey, mustard and sugar, spread over the fat and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, basting once, until sticky and golden.
Rest for 15 minutes before carving.
Heat the oil in a large casserole or tagine and brown the diced lamb in batches, then set aside.
Fry the sliced onions for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and spices and cook for 1 minute.
Return the lamb with the tomatoes and stock, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Add the apricots, drained chickpeas and honey and cook for a further 30 minutes until the lamb is very tender.
Season and serve scattered with coriander and toasted flaked almonds.

recipe-name: Bangers and Mash with Onion Gravy
instructions: Bake or grill the sausages for 25 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through.
Meanwhile, cook the sliced onions in the oil over a low heat for 20 minutes until soft and caramelised.
Boil the peeled potatoes for 15 to 20 minutes until tender, then mash with the butter and warm milk and season.
Stir the flour into the onions, gradually add the stock, balsamic vinegar and thyme leaves and simmer for 5 minutes until thickened.
Serve the sausages on the mash with plenty of onion gravy.
Bash the chicken breasts between two sheets of baking paper until about 1 cm thick.
Put the seasoned flour, the beaten eggs and the panko mixed with the grated parmesan in three shallow dishes.
Coat each breast in flour, then egg, then the crumbs, pressing them on firmly.
Fry two at a time in the hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until golden and cooked through.
Serve with lemon wedges and the rocket.
Take the steaks out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking, rub with the oil and season with salt.
Cook in a very hot frying pan for 2 to 3 minutes on each side for medium-rare, then rest on a warm plate.
Lower the heat, add the butter, finely chopped shallot and crushed peppercorns and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the brandy and carefully let it bubble away, then add the stock and reduce by half.
Stir in the cream and any resting juices, simmer for 2 minutes until thickened and spoon over the steaks.
Mix the yoghurt with half the lemon juice, the crushed garlic, spices and oil, add the chicken thighs and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Cook the chicken under a hot grill or on a griddle for 6 to 7 minutes on each side until charred and cooked through, then slice.
Mix the tahini with the remaining lemon juice and enough water to make a pourable sauce.
Warm the flatbreads and fill with the chicken, shredded cabbage, sliced tomatoes and pickled chillies.
Drizzle with the tahini sauce and roll up tightly.
Mix the yoghurt and spice paste, stir in the diced chicken and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Fry the sliced onions in the ghee for 15 minutes until deep golden and crisp, then remove half for the garnish.
Add the chicken and its marinade to the pan and cook for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the rinsed rice with the salt, cardamom and cinnamon for 5 minutes until part-cooked, then drain and layer over the chicken, drizzling with the saffron soaked in the warm milk.
Cover tightly and cook over a very low heat for 25 minutes, then scatter with the reserved onions and the herbs.
Slice the steak very thinly across the grain.
Blend or grate the pear, garlic and ginger, then mix with the soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil.
Toss the beef in the marinade and leave for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Stir-fry the beef in batches in the vegetable oil over a very high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until caramelised, then serve over the rice topped with sliced spring onions and sesame seeds.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Put the halved potatoes, chunked peppers, onion wedges and whole garlic cloves in a large roasting tin, toss with the oil and paprika and season.
Nestle in the chicken thighs, skin-side up, and scatter over the sliced chorizo.
Roast for 30 minutes, then add the tomatoes and roast for a further 15 to 20 minutes until the chicken is golden and cooked through.
Scatter with oregano leaves and serve straight from the tin.

recipe-name: Grilled Mackerel with Lemon and Herbs
instructions: Heat the grill to high and line a tray with foil.
Make three deep slashes on each side of the gutted fish.
Mash the garlic with the salt, chopped herbs, lemon zest and oil, and rub into the slashes and the cavities.
Grill for 4 to 5 minutes on each side until the skin is blistered and the flesh flakes easily.
Serve with lemon wedges.

recipe-name: Cod with Chorizo and Butter Beans
instructions: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan and fry the sliced chorizo for 3 minutes until it releases its oil.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and paprika.
Add the halved tomatoes, drained beans and stock and simmer for 5 minutes.
Nestle the seasoned cod fillets into the beans, cover and cook gently for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish flakes easily.
Stir the spinach through the beans around the fish until wilted and serve.
Heat the oil in a large pan and add the mustard seeds until they pop.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, slit chillies and ground spices and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the coconut milk, tamarind and salt and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until pink, then scatter with coriander and serve with rice.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and cook the penne for 2 minutes less than the packet instructions, then drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk and simmer until thick.
Stir in the mustard and half the grated cheese and season.
Fold the pasta, flaked tuna, sweetcorn and peas through the sauce and tip into a baking dish.
Top with the remaining cheese and bake for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Boil the potatoes until tender, then drain and mash roughly.
Poach or bake the salmon for 10 to 12 minutes until just cooked, then flake, discarding the skin.
Gently mix the potato, salmon, sliced spring onions, chopped dill and lemon zest, season and shape into eight cakes.
Dust the cakes in flour, dip in beaten egg and coat in the panko, then chill for 15 minutes.
Fry in the oil for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until golden and hot through, and serve with lemon wedges.
Finely chop the parsley, basil, capers, anchovies and garlic, or pulse briefly in a food processor.
Stir in the mustard, vinegar and extra virgin olive oil and season to make the salsa verde.
Pat the fish dry, score the skin and season.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and cook the fillets skin-side down for 3 minutes until crisp, then turn and cook for 1 minute more.
Serve the fish with the salsa verde spooned over.
Toss the fish in the spices with 1 tbsp of the oil and season.
Finely shred the cabbage and toss with the juice of one lime and a pinch of salt.
Mix the soured cream with the chipotle paste.
Fry the fish in the remaining oil for 3 minutes on each side until cooked, then break into large flakes.
Warm the tortillas and fill with the fish, slaw, sliced avocado and chipotle cream, then finish with coriander and wedges of the remaining lime.
Melt the butter in a large pan and fry the chopped bacon for 4 minutes until starting to crisp.
Add the chopped onion and celery and cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the diced potatoes, stock and milk and simmer for 12 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the haddock in large chunks and the sweetcorn and simmer gently for 5 minutes until the fish flakes.
Season with black pepper and stir in the chopped parsley.
Toast the sourdough.
Halve the tomatoes and fry them in a little oil from the sardine tins for 2 to 3 minutes until softening.
Add the drained sardines and chilli flakes and warm through for 1 to 2 minutes, breaking the fish up slightly.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and stir through the chopped parsley.
Pile onto the toast and serve straight away.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a large pan and soften the chopped onion and garlic for 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then pour in the wine and let it bubble away.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring until each is absorbed, for about 18 minutes.
Stir in the peas and prawns and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the prawns are pink and the rice is tender.
Beat in the remaining butter, the grated parmesan, lemon zest and juice, season and scatter with mint.
Heat the oil in a large pan and gently fry the chopped onion, carrots, celery and pepper for 10 minutes.
Add the diced sweet potato, garlic and spices and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, drained beans and stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 35 minutes until the sweet potato is tender and the chilli has thickened.
Stir in the chocolate until melted and season to taste.
Serve with rice, avocado or soured cream.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large pan, soften the sliced spring onions, then add the spinach in batches until wilted.
Tip into a sieve, squeeze out as much liquid as possible and chop.
Mix the spinach with the crumbled feta, ricotta, beaten eggs, chopped dill and nutmeg and season with pepper.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan), layer half the filo in a baking dish, brushing each sheet with oil, then spread over the filling and top with the remaining filo, brushing each layer.
Score the top into portions and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until crisp and golden.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), slice the aubergines lengthways, brush with 4 tbsp of the oil and roast for 25 to 30 minutes until soft and golden.
Fry the crushed garlic in the remaining oil for 1 minute, add the passata and simmer for 15 minutes, then stir in most of the basil and season.
Spread a little sauce in a baking dish, then layer the aubergine, sauce, torn mozzarella and most of the grated parmesan, repeating until everything is used.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the remaining parmesan and scatter over the top.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until bubbling and golden, then rest for 10 minutes and serve with the remaining basil.
Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Heat the butter and oil in a large frying pan and fry the sliced onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic.
Add the sliced mushrooms and cook over a high heat for 8 minutes until golden and their liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the paprika, then the stock, and bubble for 3 minutes.
Reduce the heat, stir in the soured cream and mustard and warm through without boiling, then scatter with parsley and serve with the rice.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, then plunge into iced water, drain and blend to a smooth purée.
Cut the paneer into cubes and fry in 1 tbsp of the oil until golden, then set aside.
Heat the remaining oil, add the cumin seeds until they sizzle, then fry the chopped onion for 8 minutes and add the garlic, ginger and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, garam masala, ground coriander and salt and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the spinach purée and paneer, simmer for 3 minutes, then stir in the cream and a squeeze of lemon.

recipe-name: Pesto Pasta with Potatoes and Green Beans
instructions: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden, then cool.
Blitz the basil leaves, pine nuts, garlic and parmesan in a food processor, then gradually add the oil to make a pesto and season.
Cook the pasta in a large pan of salted boiling water, adding the thinly sliced potatoes with the pasta and the halved green beans for the final 5 minutes.
Drain, reserving a cup of the cooking water.
Toss everything with the pesto and a splash of the water until glossy.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Fry the sliced garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add the passata and simmer for 10 minutes, then stir in most of the basil and season.
Cook the gnocchi in boiling water until they float, then drain.
Stir the gnocchi into the sauce, tip into a baking dish and top with torn mozzarella and grated parmesan.
Bake for 15 minutes until bubbling and golden, then scatter with the remaining basil.
Whisk the gram flour, spices, bicarbonate of soda and salt with the cold water to make a thick batter.
Stir in the thinly sliced onion, coarsely grated potato, shredded spinach, chopped chilli and coriander until well coated.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 180°C.
Fry tablespoons of the mixture in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until crisp and deep golden.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve hot with mint raita or chutney.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the chopped onion, carrots and celery for 10 minutes, then add the garlic and sliced mushrooms for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato purée, rinsed lentils, tomatoes, stock and thyme, then simmer for 35 minutes until the lentils are tender and the sauce is thick.
Meanwhile, boil both types of potato, peeled and chunked, for 15 minutes until tender, then mash with the butter and season.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), spoon the lentil mixture into a baking dish and top with the mash.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden at the edges.
Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Heat the oil in a wok and fry the curry paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk, stock and cubed sweet potato and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the sliced pepper, baby corn, mangetout and cubed tofu and simmer for 5 minutes until the vegetables are just tender.
Season with the soy sauce and lime juice, stir in the basil and serve with the rice.

Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), line a 23 cm tart tin with the pastry, cover with baking paper and baking beans and bake blind for 15 minutes, then remove the paper and beans and bake for 5 minutes more.
Fry the chopped onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the spinach until wilted and squeeze out the excess liquid.
Whisk the eggs, cream, milk and nutmeg together and season.
Scatter the spinach mixture and grated cheddar into the pastry case and pour over the egg mixture.
Reduce the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until just set with a slight wobble, then cool for 10 minutes before slicing.
Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Cut the carrots and courgette into matchsticks and slice the mushrooms.
Stir-fry each vegetable separately in a little of the vegetable oil and half the sesame oil with a little garlic and soy sauce for 2 to 3 minutes, then set aside in separate piles.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set but the yolks are runny.
Divide the rice between bowls, arrange the vegetables on top with an egg in the centre, and serve with the gochujang thinned with the remaining sesame oil and sprinkled with sesame seeds.

recipe-name: Jacket Potatoes with Cheese and Beans
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Prick the potatoes all over with a fork, rub with the oil and salt and bake directly on the oven shelf for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes until crisp outside and soft inside.
Heat the beans in a pan for the last 5 minutes.
Cut a cross in the top of each potato, squeeze gently to open and add a knob of butter.
Spoon over the beans and top with the grated cheese.
Blend the shallots, garlic, chilli and shrimp paste to a rough paste.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a wok and fry the paste for 2 minutes, then add the thinly sliced chicken and stir-fry for 4 minutes until cooked.
Add the rice and stir-fry for 4 minutes until piping hot, then stir in the kecap manis, soy sauce and sliced spring onions.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until crisp at the edges.
Serve the rice topped with a fried egg, with sliced cucumber and tomatoes on the side.
Roughly mash the potatoes and mix with the chopped cabbage and sprouts, then season well.
Heat the butter and oil in a large non-stick frying pan and soften the chopped onion for 5 minutes.
Add the potato mixture, press down into a large cake and cook over a medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until a golden crust forms underneath.
Break up and turn the mixture in sections, press down again and cook for 5 to 8 minutes more.
Serve in wedges, ideally with a fried egg or leftover cold meats.
Thinly slice the potatoes and onion.
Heat the oil in a 24 cm non-stick frying pan and cook the potatoes and onion gently for 20 to 25 minutes, turning occasionally, until soft but not browned.
Drain the potatoes in a sieve set over a bowl, keeping the oil.
Beat the eggs with the salt, stir in the potatoes and leave for 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp of the reserved oil in the pan, add the mixture and cook gently for 8 minutes, then invert onto a plate, slide back in and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more until just set.
Coarsely grate the courgettes, toss with the salt and leave in a sieve for 10 minutes, then squeeze out as much water as possible.
Mix the courgettes with the sliced spring onions, crumbled feta, beaten eggs, flour, half the chopped mint and the lemon zest, and season with pepper.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and fry heaped spoonfuls of the mixture for 3 minutes on each side until golden.
Drain on kitchen paper.
Mix the yoghurt with the remaining mint and a squeeze of lemon juice and serve with the fritters.
Heat the oil in a large pan and gently fry the chopped onion, carrots and celery for 10 minutes.
Add the sliced garlic, rosemary leaves and chilli flakes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, drained beans and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, lightly crushing some of the beans to thicken.
Stir in the shredded kale and cook for 5 minutes until tender.
Squeeze in the lemon juice, season and serve topped with grated parmesan.
Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and rub a baking dish with the butter.
Peel the potatoes and slice them very thinly, ideally on a mandoline.
Bring the cream, milk, crushed garlic, nutmeg and salt to a simmer, add the potatoes and simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring carefully.
Tip into the dish, level the top and scatter with the grated gruyère.
Bake for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Peel the carrots and parsnips and cut into similar-sized batons.
Toss with the oil, thyme and salt and roast for 25 minutes.
Drizzle over the honey, toss well and roast for 10 to 15 minutes more until tender and sticky.
Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan).
Melt the butter in a large ovenproof casserole and soften the sliced onion for 5 minutes.
Add the finely shredded cabbage, grated apple, sugar, vinegar, spices and the zest and juice of the orange, and season.
Stir well, cover tightly and cook in the oven for 1 hour 15 minutes, stirring once or twice, until very tender.
Adjust the seasoning and serve, or cool and reheat the next day when the flavour is even better.
Rinse the rice in several changes of cold water until the water runs clear, then soak for 15 minutes and drain.
Melt the ghee in a pan with a tight-fitting lid and fry the whole spices and bay leaf for 1 minute.
Add the finely sliced onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden.
Stir in the rice, turmeric and salt, then pour in the boiling water.
Cover and cook over a very low heat for 12 minutes, then turn off the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes before fluffing up with a fork.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Scrub the sweet potatoes and cut into wedges, leaving the skins on.
Toss with the oil, paprika, garlic granules and salt and spread out in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and crisp at the edges.
Scatter with snipped chives before serving.
Heat the oil in a large pan or wok over a medium heat and fry the sliced garlic for 1 minute until just golden.
Add the spinach in large handfuls, tossing until each batch wilts before adding the next.
Season with the salt and chilli flakes.
Tip into a sieve to drain off any excess liquid, then squeeze over the lemon juice and serve straight away.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), line a 23 cm tart tin with the pastry and bake blind for 15 minutes, then remove the paper and beans and bake for 5 minutes more.
Reduce the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Gently warm the golden syrup in a pan until runny, then stir in the breadcrumbs, lemon zest and juice and ginger.
Beat the cream and egg together and stir into the syrup mixture, then pour into the pastry case.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until just set and golden, then cool for at least 20 minutes before serving with clotted cream or custard.
Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan) and draw a 22 cm circle on a sheet of baking paper on a baking tray.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, then whisk in the sugar a spoonful at a time until thick and glossy, and fold in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla.
Spread the meringue inside the circle, making a slight dip in the centre, then reduce the oven to 120°C (100°C fan) and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Turn off the oven and leave the meringue inside with the door ajar until completely cool.
Whip the cream to soft peaks, spoon onto the meringue and top with the berries and passion fruit pulp just before serving.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), line a 23 cm tart tin with the pastry and bake blind for 15 minutes, then remove the paper and beans and bake for 5 minutes more.
Reduce the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and spread the jam over the base of the pastry case.
Beat the butter and caster sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs, ground almonds and almond extract.
Spread the frangipane over the jam, scatter with the flaked almonds and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden and firm to the touch.
Cool in the tin and dust with icing sugar before serving.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water, then cool slightly.
Separate the eggs and stir the yolks into the chocolate one at a time.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold into the chocolate.
Whisk the egg whites with the salt to soft peaks, then whisk in the sugar until glossy and fold into the chocolate mixture in three batches.
Spoon into six glasses and chill for at least 3 hours until set.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), line a 23 cm tart tin with the pastry and bake blind for 15 minutes, then remove the paper and beans and bake for 5 minutes more.
Mix the cornflour, 150 g of the sugar and the lemon zest and juice in a pan, gradually stir in the water and cook, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Remove from the heat, beat in the egg yolks and butter, then pour into the pastry case.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, then gradually whisk in the remaining sugar until thick and glossy and spread over the filling, sealing it to the pastry edge.
Reduce the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and bake for 20 minutes until the meringue is golden, then cool for at least 1 hour before slicing.
Crush the biscuits to fine crumbs, mix with the melted butter and press firmly into the base of a 23 cm springform tin, then chill for 15 minutes.
Beat the cream cheese, icing sugar, vanilla and lemon zest until smooth.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold into the cream cheese mixture with the lemon juice.
Gently fold in two-thirds of the raspberries, spread over the base and smooth the top.
Chill for at least 4 hours until set, then top with the remaining raspberries before serving.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a 20 cm square tin.
Rub 175 g of the butter into the flour and caster sugar until it comes together as a dough, then press into the tin and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until pale golden, then cool.
Melt the remaining butter with the muscovado sugar and condensed milk, bring to the boil and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until thick and golden.
Pour the caramel over the shortbread and leave to set for 30 minutes.
Melt the chocolate, pour over the caramel and leave to set completely before cutting into 16 squares.
Sift the flour, bicarbonate of soda and spices into a bowl and rub in the butter until it resembles breadcrumbs, then stir in the sugar.
Beat the egg with the golden syrup, add to the bowl and mix to a smooth dough.
Wrap and chill for 15 minutes, then heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line two baking trays.
Roll out to 5 mm thick on a lightly floured surface and cut out shapes, re-rolling the trimmings.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until golden, then cool on the trays for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.
Rub the butter into the flour and mixed spice until it resembles breadcrumbs, then stir in 85 g of the sugar and the currants.
Beat in the egg and enough milk to make a firm dough.
Roll out on a lightly floured surface to 5 mm thick and cut out rounds with a 6 cm cutter.
Cook on a lightly greased griddle or heavy frying pan over a low to medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes on each side until golden but still soft in the middle.
Dust with the remaining sugar while warm.
Peel the pears, leaving the stalks on, and cut a thin slice from the base so they stand upright.
Put the wine, sugar, cinnamon, star anise, strips of orange zest and the split vanilla pod in a pan just big enough to hold the pears, and heat until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pears, cover with a circle of baking paper and simmer gently for 20 to 30 minutes, turning occasionally, until tender to the point of a knife.
Lift out the pears, then boil the liquid until reduced to a syrupy consistency.
Serve the pears warm or cold with the syrup spooned over.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and dust a baking tray with flour.
Mix both flours, the bicarbonate of soda and salt in a large bowl.
Make a well in the centre, pour in the buttermilk and mix quickly with a knife to a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Shape into a round on a floured surface without kneading too much, put on the tray and cut a deep cross in the top.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the loaf sounds hollow when tapped underneath, then cool on a wire rack.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray.
Mix the sausage meat with the finely chopped onion, chopped herbs and plenty of black pepper.
Cut the pastry in half lengthways and lay a sausage of the meat along the centre of each strip.
Brush one edge with beaten egg, fold the pastry over and press to seal, then cut each roll into six pieces.
Brush with more of the egg, sprinkle with the fennel seeds and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until puffed and golden.
Peel the mango and cut the flesh away from the stone.
Blend the mango with the yoghurt, milk, honey and cardamom until smooth.
Add the ice and blend again briefly.
Pour into two glasses and serve straight away.
Heat the milk in a pan until steaming but not boiling.
Whisk in the finely chopped chocolate, cocoa and sugar until completely smooth.
Add the vanilla and cinnamon and simmer gently for 2 minutes, whisking until frothy.
Pour into mugs and serve with marshmallows or whipped cream if you like.
